tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: M. K. Stalin
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.current_position: Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, President of DMK
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.education: B.A. in History from Presidency College, Chennai
political_journey: 1967: Campaigned for DMK at the age of 14
1976: Incarcerated under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) during the Emergency
1989: Elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly for the first time from Thousand Lights
1996-2002: Served as the first directly elected Mayor of Chennai
2006-2011: Served as Minister for Rural Development and Local Administration
2009-2011: Served as Deputy Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu
2018: Elected as the President of DMK following the demise of his father, M. Karunanidhi
2021: Became the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Edappadi K. Palaniswami
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.political_party: All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK)
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.current_position: General Secretary of AIADMK, Leader of the Opposition
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.education: B.Sc (discontinued) from Sri Vasavi College, Erode
political_journey: 1974: Joined AIADMK
1989: Elected to Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly for the first time from Edappadi constituency
1998: Elected as Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from Tiruchengode
2011-2016: Served as Minister for Highways and Minor Ports
2017: Sworn in as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu
2021: Became Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly
2023: Officially recognized as the General Secretary of AIADMK

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Nainar Nagendran
political_journey: 2001: Elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly from Tirunelveli constituency as an AIADMK candidate
2001-2006: Served as Minister for Electricity and Industries in the Jayalalithaa cabinet
2017: Joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)
2021: Won the Tirunelveli assembly seat again, becoming the BJP Legislative Party Leader in Tamil Nadu
2024-2026: Rose to lead the state unit as the State President

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: K. Selvaperunthagai
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.current_position: State President, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee
political_journey: 2006: Elected as MLA from Mangalore constituency on a VCK ticket
2010: Joined the Indian National Congress
2021: Elected as MLA from Sriperumbudur constituency on an INC ticket and became the Congress Legislature Party leader
2024: Appointed as the President of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC)

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Seeman
political_journey: 1990s-2000s: Worked as a film director and actor in Tamil cinema
2009: Emerged as a prominent activist during the Sri Lankan Tamil civil war protests
2010: Founded the Naam Tamilar Katchi (We Tamils Party)
2016: Led the party in its first state assembly election
2021: Positioned NTK as the third-largest party in Tamil Nadu by vote share, independently fielding candidates in all 234 constituencies

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Anbumani Ramadoss
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.education: M.B.B.S. from Madras Medical College, Chennai
political_journey: 2004: Entered active politics and became a Rajya Sabha MP
2004-2009: Served as the Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, famously initiating the ban on smoking in public places and implementing the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)
2014-2019: Served as Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from Dharmapuri
2022: Unanimously elected as the President of the PMK

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Thol. Thirumavalavan
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.education: B.Sc, B.L., M.A. in Criminology, Ph.D.
political_journey: 1980s: Worked as a forensic assistant in the government sector before turning to full-time activism
1990: Took leadership of the Dalit Panthers of India (DPI) in Tamil Nadu
1999: Rebranded DPI as a mainstream political party, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK)
2001: Elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly for the first time
2009, 2019, 2024: Elected as Member of Parliament to the Lok Sabha from Chidambaram

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Premalatha Vijayakanth
political_journey: 2005: Played a foundational role alongside her husband, actor Vijayakanth, in launching the DMDK
2006-2023: Served as a key strategist, core committee member, and star campaigner for the party
2023: Unanimously elected as the General Secretary of DMDK due to Vijayakanth's declining health
2024-2026: Continues to lead the party following the demise of its founder in December 2023

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Vaiko
tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.education: B.A. Economics, M.A., B.L. (Madras Law College)
political_journey: 1978: Elected to the Rajya Sabha for the first time as a DMK member, serving for many years
1993: Expelled from the DMK due to internal party differences
1994: Founded the Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK)
1998, 1999: Elected to the Lok Sabha from Sivakasi constituency
2019: Elected again to the Rajya Sabha

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Vijay
political_journey: 1992-2023: Established a massive fanbase as a leading actor in Tamil cinema
2009: Launched his fan club 'Vijay Makkal Iyakkam' which engaged in extensive social welfare activities
2021: His fan club members contested and won several seats in local body elections as independents
2024: Officially founded the political party Tamizhaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in February
2026: Leading TVK in its first-ever Legislative Assembly elections

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: Kamal Haasan
political_journey: 1960-Present: Achieved legendary status as a pan-Indian actor, filmmaker, and cultural icon
2018: Launched Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) as a centrist political alternative
2019: Led MNM in the Lok Sabha elections where the party secured a noticeable vote share in urban pockets
2021: Contested from Coimbatore South assembly constituency but narrowly lost
2024: Allied with the DMK-led bloc for the national elections

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: T. T. V. Dhinakaran
political_journey: 1999: Elected as a Member of Parliament to the Lok Sabha from Periyakulam on an AIADMK ticket
2004: Elected to the Rajya Sabha
2017: Won the Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar by-election as an independent candidate following Jayalalithaa's death
2018: Launched his own political outfit, Amma Makkal Munnettra Kazagam (AMMK), to reclaim Jayalalithaa's legacy

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: G. K. Vasan
political_journey: 2001: Entered active politics following the death of his father, the veteran Congress leader G. K. Moopanar
2002: Merged the original TMC back into the Indian National Congress
2006-2014: Served as a Union Cabinet Minister in the UPA government
2014: Split from the INC and revived the Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar)
2020: Elected to the Rajya Sabha

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: K. Krishnasamy
political_journey: 1990s: Emerged as a strong voice for marginalized communities, particularly fighting for the rights of the Devendrakula Velalar community
1996: Elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly as an independent candidate from Ottapidaram
1997: Founded the political party Puthiya Tamilagam (PT)
2011: Elected again as an MLA from Ottapidaram, securing further recognition for his advocacy

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: R. Mutharasan
political_journey: 1970s: Began his political career working extensively with the Tamil Nadu Agricultural Workers Union
1980s-1990s: Led numerous statewide agitations demanding fair rights for farmers, landless laborers, and minimum wages
2015: Elected as the State Secretary of CPI in Tamil Nadu, succeeding D. Pandian
2021: Played a crucial role in the Secular Progressive Alliance, ensuring electoral success for the party

tamil_nadu_political_leaders_bio.name: K. Balakrishnan
political_journey: 1970s: Entered politics through the Students' Federation of India (SFI) and served as its State President
1989-2010: Served as the President of the Tamil Nadu Farmers Association, participating in several mass struggles
2011: Elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly from the Chidambaram constituency
2018: Elected as the State Secretary of CPI(M) Tamil Nadu
